climate.overview_html: The WMO's latest climate bulletin confirms July 2026 as the joint-warmest July on record — tying July 2024 — and likely the single warmest month in the instrumental record since 1850, as El Niño-supercharged extra-polar sea surface temperatures hit an all-time July high. In the US, Louisiana wildfires are actively burning in Winn Parish; the NIFC's August outlook warns of above-normal significant fire potential across the Gulf South through fall, even as the overall US season has already consumed 5.3 million acres — well above the 10-year average of 3.7 million. ESA's 2026 compound-crisis synthesis documents wildfire, drought, and extreme heat simultaneously at satellite-era records across three continents.

items.headline: July 2026 Joint-Warmest July on Record; Extra-Polar Sea Surface Temperatures Hit All-Time High for July
items.summary: July 2026 tied July 2024 as the warmest July in the instrumental record; the WMO assesses it as more likely than not the warmest individual month globally since 1850. Sea surface temperatures over extra-polar oceans reached their highest level ever recorded for any July, partly reflecting the intensifying El Niño. Concurrent extreme heat, prolonged drought, and flooding events worldwide signal an unprecedented compound-crisis summer.

items.headline: Louisiana Wildfires 2026: Active Fires in Winn Parish as Flash Drought Expands Across Gulf South
items.summary: The Cluster Fire (1,122 acres) and Sunset Fire (1,000+ acres) are active in Winn County. NIFC's August seasonal outlook forecasts above-normal significant fire potential across Louisiana, Mississippi, and adjacent states through fall, citing flash-drought conditions driven by extreme heat, dry air, and minimal rainfall — matching conditions that fuelled the early-season spike nationwide.

items.headline: ESA's 2026 Compound-Crisis Satellite Synthesis: Wildfire, Drought, and Extreme Heat Simultaneously at Records Across Three Continents
items.summary: ESA's Earth observation synthesis shows fire radiative power, soil moisture deficit, and land surface temperature all simultaneously at satellite-era records in 2026 across Europe, North America, and parts of Asia — a co-occurrence pattern without precedent in the full satellite archive. The report frames 2026 as the year when the cascading risk model projected for the 2030s arrived ahead of schedule.

items.headline: Europe 2026: 505,000+ Hectares Burned, Rivers at Record Lows as Drought and Heat Compound
items.summary: Wildfire burnt area already exceeds 2025 pace. Loire, Po, Rhine, and Danube at record-low flows. Extreme fire danger stretches from Germany through Poland to the Balkans. JRC attributes the compound severity to persistent drought overlapping with record-frequency heatwave recurrence.

items.headline: Record El Niño Could Fast-Forward Planet's Temperature by a Decade
items.summary: WMO forecasts +2.9°C Pacific SST anomaly for ASO 2026. Combination of El Niño, anomalously hot background ocean temperatures, and jet-stream changes is temporarily pushing global surface temperatures to levels otherwise expected in the late 2030s.

items.headline: Extraordinary ENSO Diagnostic: Subsurface Pacific Heat Reaches +10°C; 69% Probability of All-Time Record El Niño
items.summary: Subsurface temperature anomalies in the central equatorial Pacific exceed +10°C at depth — the largest warm pool in the modern observational record. CPC assigns 69% probability that the 2026/27 event will peak above every prior El Niño since 1950.

items.headline: August 2026 Tracking as Third-Warmest August on Record; SW Europe Posts Most Intense Heat Anomaly in ERA5 History
items.summary: SW Europe posts its most intense August heat anomaly in the ERA5 record back to 1940. Broad marine heatwave conditions persist across the Mediterranean and North Atlantic, further reducing the atmosphere's capacity to moderate land-surface temperatures.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Lala — Post-Hawaii, Central Pacific
major_events.impact: Battered the Hawaiian Big Island with 40+ inches of rain and near-hurricane-force winds; 100+ homes damaged or destroyed. Now spinning westward over open ocean and expected to re-intensify in lower-shear waters west of the island chain.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Saudel (17W) — Approaching Northern Marianas
major_events.impact: Track forecast to pass within 6 nm of Agrihan and 26 nm of Pagan this Saturday. Rapid intensification expected in record-warm SSTs with minimal wind shear; super-typhoon potential on the extended track.

major_events.name: US South Heat Dome — Texas to Carolinas
major_events.impact: Heat indices 110–115°F through August 21; dozens of daily and all-time records threatened across TX, GA, SC, FL panhandle.

major_events.name: Midwest Severe Storms and Flash Flooding
major_events.impact: Stalled frontal boundary and Gulf moisture triggering multi-day flooding across Plains and Midwest. Prior derecho hit Indiana with 99 mph gusts and widespread structural damage; Level 2/5 severe risk continued Aug 18–19 for Nebraska, Iowa, northern Missouri.

weather.overview_html: Tropical Storm Lala made a damaging pass over the Hawaiian Islands, lashing the Big Island with near-hurricane-force winds and more than 40 inches of rain — destroying or damaging over 100 homes — before weakening and spinning westward; it is expected to re-intensify over open ocean well west of Hawaii. In the western Pacific, Tropical Storm Saudel (17W) is on track to reach typhoon strength and pass dangerously close to Agrihan and Pagan in the Northern Marianas this Saturday, with super-typhoon potential still on the table for its extended track. Over the US, multi-day severe storms and flash flooding continue across the Plains and Midwest as a stalled front and Gulf moisture funnelling combine to keep the threat pinned in place, while the Southern heat dome holds 70+ million under heat alerts through August 21.

items.source: NPR / Civil Beat / NASA Earth Observatory
items.headline: Tropical Storm Lala Batters Hawaii's Big Island — 100+ Structures Damaged, Record Rainfall in Valleys
items.summary: Lala weakened from CAT 2 to tropical storm as it tracked over cooler nearshore waters but still delivered wind gusts near 80 mph and rainfall exceeding 40 inches in some Big Island valleys. More than 100 structures damaged or destroyed. Visitor operations largely returning to normal; system now spinning west-northwest and expected to re-intensify in lower-shear, warmer waters away from the island chain.

items.headline: TS Saudel (17W) Expected to Reach Typhoon Strength by Friday, Close Pass to Northern Marianas Saturday
items.summary: As of 19/0600Z, Saudel was near 8.5°N 154.1°E with 35-kt winds, rapidly organizing without an inner core. Forecast center pass: within 6 nm of Agrihan and 26 nm of Pagan by Saturday evening. Rapid intensification expected in record-warm SSTs and less than 5-kt wind shear. Super-typhoon potential remains in extended-range guidance.

items.headline: US South Heat Dome: 70+ Million Under Alerts Through August 21 as Heat Indices Top 115°F
items.summary: Heat indices 110–115°F from Memphis to the Florida Panhandle, coastal South Carolina, and southern Georgia. Dozens of daily and some all-time records threatened through August 21. Prolonged exposure risk highest for outdoor workers and those without air conditioning in rural areas.

items.headline: Midwest Flash Flooding and Severe Storms: Stalled Front + Gulf Moisture Lock Multi-Day Threat in Place
items.summary: A Level 2/5 severe risk spans Nebraska, Iowa, and northern Missouri, with large hail and isolated tornadoes possible alongside the flooding threat. A prior derecho produced 99 mph gusts in Gary, Indiana, and widespread flash flooding across Indiana. Stalled frontal boundary expected to extend the threat zone through the weekend.

renewables.overview_html: Europe's renewables sector is in active consolidation: TotalEnergies agreed to acquire Shell's entire European onshore renewables business (4 GW of assets and pipeline across Italy, UK, and Spain) while simultaneously recycling capital via a KKR co-investment; in the US, MN8 Energy is acquiring Greenbacker for $375M to create a 6 GW national platform. Both deals are detailed in Industry News. ACCIONA Energía announced 33 MW of new BESS capacity in Spain, while in the US the battery storage interconnection backlog continues to deepen as transformer shortages dominate project timelines.

items.headline: ACCIONA Energía Plans 33 MW of Battery Storage Across Two New Spanish Projects
items.summary: Two BESS projects to strengthen renewable integration and grid stability in Spain, targeting operational start by end-2027. Part of ACCIONA's accelerating push to co-locate storage with its solar and wind fleet and capture ancillary-services revenue as Spain's grid management challenges intensify under high VRE penetration.

items.headline: Revolution Wind Now 95% Complete — 61 of 65 Turbines Installed Off Connecticut
items.summary: Final four turbines on track to close out before year-end, bringing the project to full commercial operation and delivering on a $2.9B development first announced in 2019. One of only two US offshore wind projects to reach near-completion in 2026, following the federal buyout program that removed most competing projects.

items.headline: US Big Battery Projects Pile Up as Grid Upgrade Delays Stall Interconnection
items.summary: Con Edison reports 300% growth in storage projects awaiting connection over two years. LFP cell prices at $55–75/kWh — below most analyst expectations — but transformer shortages and multi-year interconnection queue timelines, not economics, are the primary bottleneck. Grid hardware supply chains remain the critical path for the US storage build-out.

items.headline: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners Closes Growth Markets Fund II at $3B — Largest Emerging-Market Clean-Energy Close of 2026
items.summary: Nearly triple its predecessor fund. Targets solar, wind, storage, and grid infrastructure across 15 emerging economies. The close signals continued institutional appetite for clean energy in markets where energy access gaps and renewable potential are both highest.

science.overview_html: ECMWF's brand-new AIFS-TC preprint (arXiv:2608.09959) shows that a two-component ML correction — AIFS predicts intensity, a second network corrects AIFS's systematic underestimation bias — reaches the operational frontier for tropical cyclone maximum wind speed and minimum central pressure at leads from 12 hours to seven days; the entire system was reportedly designed and built by an LLM (Claude Fable 5) under single-scientist direction in a matter of hours. The companion AIFS-SUBS preprint extends data-driven forecasting to sub-seasonal timescales, beating operational IFS by eight days on MJO skill. Meanwhile, the WP-MIP international intercomparison project now has 11 institutions contributing AI, hybrid, and NWP model forecasts to establish the first rigorously standardized evaluation across paradigms.

items.headline: AIFS-TC: A Simple AI Correction Reaches the Operational Frontier for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Forecasting
items.summary: A two-component system: AIFS-Single provides an initial intensity estimate, and a second ML model trained on AIFS's historical errors applies a learned correction, addressing the persistent low-bias common to AI weather models on TC intensity. Tested on 2025 TC season cases, the combined system matches both leading operational guidance and the current AI state-of-the-art on maximum wind speed and minimum central pressure at 12-h to 7-day leads. The full system was reportedly built by Claude Fable 5 in hours under a single scientist's natural-language direction.

items.headline: AIFS-SUBS: Extending ECMWF's Data-Driven Forecasting to Sub-Seasonal Timescales
items.summary: Adapts AIFS-CRPS with a 24-hour autoregressive time step to reduce error accumulation across week-2 to week-4 leads; adds stratospheric levels and top-of-atmosphere thermal radiation as predictors. Extends skillful MJO forecasts by eight days beyond the operational IFS and reproduces observed MJO modulation of tropical cyclone activity at comparable fidelity. Part of ECMWF's AI Weather Quest initiative with 60+ competing sub-seasonal AI models worldwide.

items.headline: WP-MIP: International AI, Hybrid, and Physical Weather Model Intercomparison Project Launches With 11 Institutions Across Six Continents
items.summary: WMO-supported initiative creating a centralized database of AI, hybrid, and NWP model forecasts initialized from both center-specific and common conditions, enabling the first rigorously controlled head-to-head evaluation. AI-ready verification techniques will identify the strengths and weaknesses of each class of prediction system, providing best-practice guidance to model developers and national weather centers globally.

items.headline: ECMWF: Building Shared Foundations for Machine-Learned Weather Prediction
items.summary: ECMWF's ML project coordinates shared models, datasets, and infrastructure to accelerate research-to-operations. 2026 milestones include the first operational AIFS sub-seasonal model and the AI Weather Quest competition with more than 60 sub-seasonal AI models under development by international teams. ECMWF also upgraded AIFS Single and AIFS ENS in parallel with IFS Cycle 50r1, adding snow output and improved scores.

items.headline: State of the Climate in 2025: Record Greenhouse Gases, Sea Level, and Ocean Heat
items.summary: 2025 ranks among the three warmest years since 1850 despite a fading La Niña. Every major climate indicator — CO₂, CH₄, sea level, ocean heat — set new records for the second consecutive year. Copernicus and NOAA contributed key data streams.

items.headline: Rate of Warming, Not Just Temperature Level, Determines AMOC Collapse Risk
items.summary: Slow CO₂ ramps keep AMOC stable past +5.5°C; fast ramps collapse it at +2°C. Finding reframes risk assessment: stabilization rate and trajectory matter as much as the endpoint temperature target, with implications for how emergency overshoot scenarios are evaluated in integrated assessment models.

items.headline: AIFS Single 1.1.0: Formal Peer-Reviewed Validation of ECMWF's Machine-Learned Weather Forecast Model
items.summary: Hard physical-consistency constraints in training substantially improve precipitation skill. Soil moisture and energy-flux variables added. Consistent 4–6% improvements across lead times and variables vs. AIFS 1.0. First peer-reviewed publication for any operational ECMWF AI forecast model.

items.title: TotalEnergies Acquires Shell's Entire European Onshore Renewables Business — 4 GW of Assets and Pipeline Across Italy, UK, and Spain
items.body_html: TotalEnergies announced two simultaneous European transactions: (1) acquisition of Shell's entire European onshore renewables business — 500 MW of solar and wind operating or under construction (mainly Italy and Netherlands) plus a 3.5 GW development pipeline in Italy, UK, and Spain; and (2) sale of a 50% stake in a separate 1.2 GW portfolio of developed assets to a KKR-managed insurance account at €1.8B enterprise value, effectively recycling capital. TotalEnergies' European renewables portfolio now approaches 10 GW installed or under construction. Both transactions are expected to close by year-end, subject to regulatory approvals. The deal underscores accelerating exit pressure on oil majors' European renewable minority positions.

items.title: MN8 Energy to Acquire Greenbacker Renewable Energy for $375M, Creating One of the Three Largest US Clean Power Platforms at 6 GW
items.body_html: MN8 Energy Holdings agreed to acquire Greenbacker Renewable Energy Company LLC in a cash-and-equity deal valued at up to $375M ($350M at close + up to $25M contingent on commercial milestones). The combination creates a 6.2 GW national fleet across 33 states spanning utility-scale solar, onshore wind, distributed generation, and battery storage — one of the three largest US clean energy operators. Strategic rationale: capturing the surge in data-center and electrification power demand with full lifecycle control over development, financing, and asset management. Transaction expected to close Q4 2026, subject to Greenbacker shareholder approval.

items.title: Form Energy Raises $750M Series G to Scale Iron-Air Battery Manufacturing
items.body_html: Form Energy, maker of 100-hour iron-air batteries, closed a $750M Series G led by T. Rowe Price, with Sequoia Capital and Franklin Templeton joining. Total equity raised now exceeds $2B. Commercial backlog quadrupled in 2026 to 80 GWh, with signed contracts from Xcel Energy and Google. Iron-air batteries' ability to deliver 100-hour continuous discharge at low cost positions the company as a key candidate for seasonal storage and multi-day grid resilience applications.

items.title: Renew Risk Launches First Catastrophe Models Purpose-Built for Offshore Wind Farms — Europe and US Solar Editions Now Live
items.body_html: Renew Risk released its UK & Ireland Windstorm Model (UKWS) and European Windstorm Model (EUWS) in April 2026 — the first catastrophe models engineered specifically for offshore wind farms, using at-sea wind speed data, extreme wave impacts, and asset-level detail (turbines, inter-array cables, substations) with forward-looking coverage through 2032. A US solar storm catastrophe model followed in May. The company claims nine-month development cycles versus the industry's typical three years. Nasdaq distributes the models as part of its risk-analytics platform. As offshore turbines reach 160–230 m height and face a changing storm environment, traditional onshore-proxy models have been materially underpricing offshore exposures.
